skill.name: webask-quiz-timeline
skill.description: Показывает историю опроса WebAsk во времени: когда его публиковали, когда шли ответы, где всплески и провалы. Применяется, когда человек спрашивает, почему ответы прекратились, что изменилось или как шёл сбор за период.
skill.summary: Compare WebAsk survey response trends with publication history to investigate drops, spikes, and collection gaps.
skill.author: webaskio

SKILL.md line 18 formats get_quiz_versions as inline Markdown code when describing publication snapshots. There is no executable backtick expression or shell command in this context.

content.value_statement: Survey response drops are difficult to explain without knowing when the survey changed. This skill compares response trends with publication history and checks integrations.
actual_capabilities: Request date-filtered survey reports with daily or weekly response groupings.
Retrieve publication snapshots to identify when survey versions changed.
Compare response drops, spikes, and gradual declines with publication dates.
Check integration status and investigate publication status when responses suddenly stop.
Summarize key dates and plausible explanations while acknowledging unsupported causal links.
limitations: Requires access to the WebAsk MCP tools get_quiz_report, get_quiz_versions, and get_quiz_integrations.
Matching dates alone cannot prove that a survey edit caused a response change.
Advertising, email campaigns, and other external events require context beyond the listed survey tools.
The workflow is read-only and does not repair survey logic, republish surveys, or change integrations.

use_cases.title: Investigate Campaign Response Drops
use_cases.description: Compare survey response declines with publication dates and supplied campaign events to identify plausible explanations.

use_cases.title: Review Survey Revision Effects
use_cases.description: Compare response activity before and after survey publications to identify changes that warrant investigation.

use_cases.title: Triage Stopped Response Collection
use_cases.description: Review response timing, integration status, and publication status when a survey suddenly stops receiving submissions.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Recent Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how responses to WebAsk survey [survey] changed during [date range]. Summarize the main dates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review response activity over a defined period.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Responses and Publications
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare daily responses to [survey] with its publication history during [date range]. Identify drops and spikes near publication dates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect response trends with survey changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Sudden Stop
prompt_templates.prompt: Responses to [survey] stopped around [date]. Review reports, publication history, integration status, and whether the survey remains published. Distinguish evidence from hypotheses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate an abrupt decline to zero responses.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Competing Explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [survey] during [date range] alongside these campaign events: [events]. Choose daily or weekly grouping and account for weekday patterns. Compare explanations without assuming causation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine survey evidence with supplied external context.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: explain the late-August decline using the sample response counts and publication history.
output: August 18-24: 31 responses; a new version was published on August 19.
September 1-7: 74 responses after a logic correction on September 1.
The publication and recovery dates support investigating the earlier logic change; timing alone does not establish the cause.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: responses declined without survey edits, and no campaign information is available.
output: The response decline does not coincide with a publication change.
Campaign timing or audience activity could explain the decline, but supporting evidence is missing.
Conclusion: the available survey history does not establish why responses fell.

best_practices: Specify the survey and date range before requesting a timeline.
Provide known campaign dates and compare equivalent weekdays when interpreting response trends.
Treat date matches as hypotheses until survey changes or other evidence support a causal explanation.
anti_patterns: Assuming every response decline was caused by the latest publication.
Comparing weekday and weekend response counts without noting weekly patterns.
Expecting the read-only analysis workflow to modify surveys or resolve account limits.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It compares WebAsk survey response activity with publication history and checks integrations when collection suddenly stops.

faq.question: Which tools must be available?
faq.answer: The skill depends on get_quiz_report, get_quiz_versions, and get_quiz_integrations through WebAsk MCP.

faq.question: Can it prove why responses stopped?
faq.answer: Not always. It identifies plausible relationships and should report when the available evidence does not establish a cause.

faq.question: Will it change my survey?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses read-only tools and does not edit or republish surveys.

faq.question: Does it use daily or weekly response counts?
faq.answer: The instructions select daily or weekly grouping based on the collection period.

faq.question: Which language does it use for its response?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to respond in the language used by the requester.
